label: thm1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm1}
Let $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ be a sequence in $GL(X)$. Then the following statements are equivalent.
\vskip3pt
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\roman*)},itemindent=1em]
\item[\rm (i)] $(T_n)_{n\in \mathbb Z}$ has the shadowing property.
\vskip2pt
\item[\rm (ii)] $(T_n)_{n\in \mathbb Z}$ is generalized pseudo-hyperbolic.
\vskip2pt
\item[\rm (iii)] $(T_n)_{n\in \mathbb Z}$ is topologically stable. 
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: thm2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm2}
Let $T\in GL(X)$. Then the following statements are equivalent.
\vskip3pt
\begin{enumerate}[label={(\roman*)},itemindent=1em]
\item[\rm (i)] $T$ has the shadowing property.
\vskip2pt
\item[\rm (ii)] $T$ is surjectively hyperbolic.
\vskip2pt
\item[\rm (iii)] $T$ is generalized pseudo-hyperbolic.
\vskip2pt
\item[\rm (iv)] $T$ is topologically stable.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ be the constant sequence defined by
$T_n:=T$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z$.
The shadowing property of~$T$ implies that the constant sequence
$(T_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ also has the shadowing property. Let
$\eta>0$ be given by Theorem~\ref{thm3}. Choose
\begin{equation*}
0<\tilde\eta<\min\left\{\eta,\frac1{\|T^{-1}\|}\right\}.
\end{equation*}
Let $f$ be a Lipschitz self-map of~$X$ such that
$\operatorname{Lip}(f)<\tilde\eta$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\|T^{-1}\|\operatorname{Lip}(f)<1,
\end{equation*}
and hence, by Remark~\ref{rem2},
\begin{equation*}
F:=T+f\in Homeo(X).
\end{equation*}
Now consider the constant sequence
$f_n:=f$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z$.
Since
\begin{equation*}
\operatorname{Lip}(f_n)=\operatorname{Lip}(f)<\tilde\eta<\eta
\qquad\text{for all $n\in\mathbb Z$},
\end{equation*}
Theorem~\ref{thm3} implies that the constant sequence
$F_n:=T_n+f_n=F$, $n\in\mathbb Z$
has the shadowing property. By Definitions~\ref{autshad} and~\ref{nonautshad}, the shadowing property of~$F$ is equivalent to that of the associated constant sequence $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$.
 Therefore, $F$ has the shadowing property.
